value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Swarm Nodes</h1><p>These nodes are all running an NGiNX Proxy manager on ports 81 (for admin) and 80 / 443 for web access to proxy client applications such as Portainer or Crafty, etc.&nbsp; Really, only one copy needs to be running, since the overlay network that it is attached to allows any node in the swarm to answer the call and direct trafic to the div.p: This is the overlay network created for NGiNX Proxy Manager. Allowing all member services to be accessed by their service name via internal DNS.
Think of it like a VLAN using NAT.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 139px; height: 1px; padding-top: 636px; margin-left: 122px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; max-height: 306px; overflow: hidden; color: #4D4D4D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#4D4D4D, #ababab); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.p: These nodes are all running an NGiNX Proxy manager on ports 81 (for admin) and 80 / 443 for web access to proxy client applications such as Portainer or Crafty, etc. Really, only one copy needs to be running, since the overlay network that it is attached to allows any node in the swarm to answer the call and direct trafic to the node that is running it.

div.p: A split DNS allows different results to DNS queries based on the source environment. Since the LAN's DHCP will handout the local DNS, it can give answers that point at private systems that are not availble outside the firewall - or even give faster/more-direct answers to things that are actually inside it anyway.
